t: You're looking at Rush Hour, a bronze group of six people walking, made in 1983 by the American artist George Segal. This is cast number three of five, standing in Exchange Square in Broadgate. It shows ordinary workers on their daily routine, and it is one of several public artworks around here that depict workers. Some people call it one of the best modern sculptures in London, while others find it depressing, because the figures are simply doing something mundane. Segal was a Pop Art sculptor and painter, awarded the United States National Medal of Arts in 1999.
